content.text:
**Cloudflare Workers has experienced multiple outages and incidents over the past year**, primarily minor in impact. These often involve API errors, elevated error rates (like 502s or 1022s), latency, timeouts, or degraded availability for specific models/features rather than full global downtime. Production-running Workers are frequently unaffected, with issues more commonly hitting deployments, APIs, KV, or AI inference.[[1]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare-workers/outage-history)

### Recent and Notable Incidents
Here are key examples from search results (as of early September 2026):

- **September 2, 2026 – Workers Issues in Narita (Japan)**: Increased errors for customers running Workers scripts in the Narita location. Detected ~1:02 AM UTC, identified and fixed by ~2:10–2:24 AM UTC (minor impact, ~1.5 hours).[[2]](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/lmsfz6pcb65c)

- **July 17, 2026 – Workers API Issues**: Errors when interacting with the Workers API/dashboard, especially during script deployment. Production Workers unaffected. Resolved within ~20 minutes.[[3]](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/km4651q3bfdf)

- **June 25–26, 2026 – Workers AI Issues**: Errors on inference requests for the `@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` model. Investigated late on the 25th, fixed and resolved by early on the 26th.[[4]](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/bpz4p8wxt2lw)

- **April 2026 (multiple)**: 
  - April 17: Elevated 502 errors in some locations (affecting Workers, Sites, CDN, R2, KV); ~28 minutes.
  - April 15: API latency (impacting builds via webhooks); ~1.5–2 hours.
  - April 13–14: KV API latency/timeouts + Assets errors; ~19 hours.[[1]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare-workers/outage-history)

- **May 2026 examples**: Workers API failures (preventing new usage, production unaffected; ~31 minutes) and Workers AI model availability issues (~1 hour).[[5]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare/incidents/582667-workers-api-issue)[[6]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare/incidents/590650-workers-ai-availability-issues)

- **March 2026**: Increased error rates for running Workers scripts; lasted ~24 hours.[[7]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare/incidents/555423-cloudflare-workers-issues)

### Major Historical Outages (2025)
Larger incidents in 2025 affected broader Cloudflare services due to dependencies on Workers KV (a key-value store used for config, auth, etc.):

- **November 18, 2025**: Triggered by a database permissions change that corrupted a Bot Management "feature file," causing widespread HTTP 5xx errors, failures in CDN/security, Turnstile, Workers KV, Access, and more. Not a cyber attack. Impact started ~11:28 UTC; mitigated over hours.[[8]](https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/)

- **June 12, 2025**: ~2.5-hour global outage hitting Workers KV (90%+ failure on uncached reads/writes), WARP, Access, Gateway, Images, Stream, Workers AI, Dashboard, etc. Root cause: Failure in underlying storage infrastructure (partly a third-party cloud provider outage). Led to architectural changes, including migrating KV storage to Cloudflare's own R2 for better resilience. No data loss or security incident.[[9]](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-service-outage-june-12-2025/)

### Patterns and Improvements
Cloudflare has responded to past major outages (e.g., Nov/Dec 2025) with "Code Orange" initiatives like "Fail Small" — segmenting the Workers runtime by customer cohorts (starting with free users), faster rollbacks, and independent services to limit blast radius. This has been in place and tested by mid-2026.[[10]](https://blog.cloudflare.com/code-orange-fail-small-complete/)

For real-time status, check [Cloudflare's official status page](https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/). Sites like [IsDown](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare-workers/outage-history) track historical reports (66 outages noted since Sept 2025, mostly minor).[[1]](https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare-workers/outage-history)

If you're experiencing a current issue or need details on a specific date/location, provide more info for a deeper search.
